subsystems.name: Print head and motion system
subsystems.role: deposits edible pastes layer by layer to build a meal.

subsystems.name: Ingredient cartridge system
subsystems.role: stores and feeds different nutrient pastes into the print head.

subsystems.name: Printable food pastes
subsystems.role: the edible 'inks' — pureed protein, carbohydrate, fat and micronutrient blends.

subsystems.name: Biometric sensor interface
subsystems.role: collects real-time data on the user's nutritional state from wearables.

subsystems.name: Recipe and control software
subsystems.role: translates nutritional targets into a printable structure and directs the machine.

subsystems.name: Post-processing unit
subsystems.role: cooks, sets or finishes the printed food so it is safe and palatable.

buildSteps.title: Formulate printable pastes
buildSteps.detail: Ingredients are cooked, pureed and blended with thickeners so each paste flows through a nozzle but holds its shape after deposition.

buildSteps.title: Load cartridges
buildSteps.detail: Each nutrient paste is filled into a separate cartridge and loaded into the printer, which may hold several at once.

buildSteps.title: Collect biometric data
buildSteps.detail: Wearable sensors stream real-time readings — such as glucose, heart rate and activity — to the printer's software.

buildSteps.title: Compute the meal plan
buildSteps.detail: Software combines the user's profile, recent intake and current biometrics to decide the proportions of protein, carbohydrate, fat and micronutrients, and the 3D structure.

buildSteps.title: Print the meal
buildSteps.detail: The print head moves over the build platform, depositing thin layers of each paste in a programmed pattern. Multi-material printing allows different textures and flavours in one item.

buildSteps.title: Post-process
buildSteps.detail: The printed item is heated, cooled or otherwise treated to set its shape, cook it safely and improve mouthfeel.

buildSteps.title: Serve and monitor
buildSteps.detail: The meal is eaten, and sensors track the body's response. That feedback can adjust the next meal's composition.

prerequisites.why: printers already exist for chocolate, dough and simple pastes, but printing a complete, safe and appetising meal from multiple nutrient streams is not yet routine.
continuous glucose monitors are widely used, but real-time sensing of the full range of nutrients the body needs is not yet available.
we know that individual responses to food vary, but the algorithms to turn wearable data into precise meal recipes are still being researched.
keeping different pastes separate, avoiding cross-contamination and cleaning the machine between meals are unresolved engineering problems.
rules for labelling, safety and health claims for automatically assembled meals do not yet exist in most countries.

pathway.milestone: single-ingredient 3D food printers and wearable glucose monitors are commercially available
pathway.unlocks: proof that edible pastes can be printed and that real-time biometric data can inform food choices.

pathway.milestone: multi-material printers that combine protein, carbohydrate, fat and micronutrient pastes in one item
pathway.unlocks: the ability to create meals with controlled composition rather than just shaped single ingredients.

pathway.milestone: integration of wearable data with printer software to suggest or automatically print a meal
pathway.unlocks: semi-automated personalised nutrition for people with specific metabolic conditions.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop systems that adjust meal composition in real time based on the body's response
pathway.unlocks: truly adaptive nutrition, though it will require advances in sensor technology, nutrition science and regulation.
